headline: Friday's rebound reverses hard — KSE-100 gives back 2,320.78 points (-1.32%) to 175,802.78 as Hormuz tension resurfaces and SBP reserves take a $1.25bn hit.
summary: The Friday session undid almost all of this week's rebound: KSE-100 closed at 175,802.78, down 2,320.78 points (-1.32%) from Thursday, as fresh US-Iran tension around the Strait of Hormuz spooked the tape again after two days of value-buying. Brent crude jumped to $85.98 (+2.1%) and the VIX rose 9% overnight, while SBP's forex reserves fell 6.7% week-on-week to $17.2bn on debt repayments — a real domestic strain, not just imported jitters. A fresh, larger fuel-price hike lands Saturday (petrol ~+Rs10, diesel ~+Rs40), adding inflation and OMC-margin pressure into next week. The desk is leaning cautious: quality banks and E&P still screen reasonably on fundamentals, but today's reversal shows how quickly Hormuz headlines can erase a rally.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Quality names (MCB, HBL, UBL) still screen cheap with 7-9% covered dividend yields and the policy rate on hold at 11.5%, but the whole group sold off again this morning with the broader index — the case is on valuation support, not price momentum.

sectors.name: E&P (Oil & Gas Exploration)
sectors.why: Brent's push to $85.98 (+2.1% today, +8.1% this month) on Hormuz risk is a direct revenue tailwind for OGDC/PPL/MARI/POL, though OGDC and PPL are both trading below their 20- and 50-day averages right now — the macro tailwind hasn't shown up in the charts yet.

sectors.name: OMCs & Refiners
sectors.why: A large fuel-price hike lands Jul 18 (petrol ~+Rs10, diesel ~+Rs40) — near-term the story is inventory/margin risk and reported diesel hoarding, and PSO's net margin is already a thin 1.4%.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-cost sensitive and among the hardest-hit sectors in this week's Hormuz selloffs; LUCK, DGKC and MLCF are all still trading below their 20-day averages despite bounce attempts.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Imported-input costs and a softer rupee squeeze margins right as the sector faces a fresh fuel-price hike and weaker consumer demand into results season.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand defensive and largely insulated from Hormuz shipping risk, but not immune — ENGROH and FFC both sold off with the broader tape this morning.

watchlist.angle: A golden cross (SMA50>SMA200) triggered today — on HCAR's own 10-trade history that setup won 60% of the time for +3.1% net (still profitable out-of-sample); entry ~Rs245.56, stop Rs233.28, target Rs270.12. Forward P/E (9.42) sits below trailing (10.71), so the market already expects earnings to improve, and results are pencilled for Jul 29.
watchlist.risk: The desk's fundamentals card rates HCAR 'caution' on a thin 2.6% net margin, and autos are one of the sectors flagged to avoid this week given the incoming fuel hike and softer rupee — a technical buy signal fighting a sector headwind.

watchlist.angle: A Williams %R mid-cross fired today, and ENGROH screens 'attractive' on fundamentals — P/E 5.3 (cheapest third of PSX), 10.2% net margin, large-cap with a low 0.05 beta. It was one of Thursday's biggest point-contributors to the rebound (+156.53 index points).
watchlist.risk: This is the desk's lowest-conviction live signal today — 63% historical hit rate but only 50% out-of-sample — and fertilizer sold off with the broader tape again this morning.

watchlist.angle: A 2-ATR stretch-below-20MA mean-reversion signal triggered today — a 69% historical win rate over 13 trades (+1.2% net, still 67% out-of-sample); entry Rs67.06, stop Rs65.05, target Rs69.74. Fundamentals are solid: 43% net margin, a covered 4.63% dividend.
watchlist.risk: NPL already jumped 7.94% on Thursday, the session's second-biggest mover — this mean-reversion setup is catching a name that's already extended, with no near-term earnings catalyst (results not until Sep 23).

watchlist.angle: Q2CY26 results landed Jul 16 — EPS of Rs1.87 and a declared Rs1.50/share dividend (book closure confirmed Jul 27, 4.93% yield). It was the day's top-volume stock (70m shares) and is still trading 3.3x average volume, holding above both its 20- and 50-day averages.
watchlist.risk: The desk's fundamentals card rates LOTCHEM 'caution' — net margin is a thin 5.5% and the dividend payout ratio is a stretched 210% of earnings; this quarter's beat looks like a standout, not (yet) a sustainable run-rate.

watchlist.angle: DCR tops the desk's predictability ranking (75.7/100, the highest on the board) and has a confirmed dividend book closure Jul 25 (Rs0.66/unit, 1.72% yield); breakout setups here have historically been reliable (Donchian-55 breakout: 71% hit rate, +3.1% net expectancy over 21 trades).
watchlist.risk: Valuation is 'expensive' (P/E 16.64) and the dividend payout ratio is a stretched 106% of earnings; this is a defensive, low-beta idea for a risk-off tape rather than a momentum trade — no technical trigger fired today.

catalysts.event: Fortnightly fuel-price review takes effect — petrol expected +~Rs10/litre, diesel +~Rs40/litre on the Hormuz oil spike
DCR book closure — confirmed final dividend of Rs0.66/unit (1.72% yield), buy-by Jul 22
SBP Monetary Policy Committee — first FY27 rate decision
LOTCHEM book closure begins — confirmed Rs1.50/share dividend (4.93% yield), buy-by Jul 24
PBS releases July 2026 CPI — first print to capture this month's fuel-price hikes and the Hormuz oil spike

risks: The US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz conflict is still live, not resolved — today's reversal shows how fast a single headline can erase two sessions of gains, and another escalation could retest Tuesday's 173,518.82 low.
SBP reserves fell $1.245bn (-6.7% WoW) to $17.226bn on external debt repayments — a real domestic funding strain sitting underneath the geopolitical noise, not just imported sentiment.
The Jul 18 fuel-price hike lands right as June CPI had just eased to 11.1% — a fresh inflation impulse could complicate the SBP's Jul 27 rate decision and pressure OMC and consumer names.
